risk_scenario: Malware or unauthorised access reaches the CTC/SCADA network through the IT to OT bridge and lets someone issue or block movement authorities
Signalling and interlocking commands are manipulated or spoofed, producing a wrong-side failure
Legacy and end-of-life OT components cannot be patched without a service possession, so known vulnerabilities stay open for long periods
Trackside and onboard IoT sensors are spoofed or tampered with and feed false telemetry into maintenance and operational decisions
Ransomware encrypts the e-ticketing and reservation platform during a peak travel period
Broken access control in the app and portal APIs exposes other passengers' bookings and personal data
Fare fraud through cloned cards, replayed QR tickets or tampered smart gate readers
Crew scheduling and rostering data is lost or corrupted, forcing manual rostering and service cancellations
Mass exfiltration of the passenger master database including identity, payment and travel history records
Cloud misconfiguration, public storage or over-permissive IAM exposes backups and operational APIs
Data poisoning or unmanaged model drift in the predictive maintenance engine causes real defects to be missed
Backups or the DR site turn out not to be recoverable when they are actually needed
CCTV cameras and recorders running default credentials or exposed to the internet are used as a foothold or for surveillance
Phishing or business email compromise leads to credential theft and lateral movement
Privileged insider misuse, or an admin account that was never revoked after someone left
Third party or supply chain compromise through vendor remote access or a poisoned software update
SOC and SIEM blind spots: OT and cloud logs are not collected, so an incident runs undetected for weeks
